In commodity markets, oil prices declined for a fourth consecutive day due to a perceived reduction in the risk of an escalation in the Iran conflict.

Cryptocurrencies experienced modest gains alongside traditional markets. Bitcoin increased by 0.60% to reach $80,660.59, while ether advanced 0.45% to trade at $2,428.15. Foreign exchange adjustments also included minor gains for the Australian and New Zealand dollars against the US currency, illustrating a broad reaction across global financial sectors to shifting political and economic indicators.

stories.title: Pakistani Cabinet Approves New Currency Designs and LPG Reforms
stories.summary:
The federal cabinet of Pakistan, presided over by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, ratified a defense cooperation agreement with Kuwait during a meeting in Islamabad. Initially signed on June 11, 2023, and ratified by Kuwait on July 19, the pact is designed to foster institutional linkages between the armed forces of both nations. During the session, the prime minister also highlighted ongoing regional diplomatic efforts aimed at easing tensions through proposed trilateral cooperation involving Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia.

To address domestic energy challenges, Prime Minister Sharif announced a transparent and competitive mechanism for allocating liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) quotas, ending a long-standing monopoly. Under the new approach, locally produced LPG will be distributed through supervised public auctions, and importing firms must follow strict procedures. Revenue raised will support public subsidies. The premier attributed local LPG supply disruptions and high prices to international petroleum costs and sea route hurdles rather than border closures. Furthermore, the government extended its fuel subsidy program until December, utilizing Rs28 billion to aid approximately 15 million citizens, though authorities were directed to penalize irregularities found at certain petrol pumps.

In provincial administration, the federal cabinet transferred the powers of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi to maintain governance following the declaration of governor's rule on October 11. Governor Kundi is required to submit monthly review reports to the federal government. Additionally, the administration finalized a comprehensive Rs160 billion security and development package for the province aimed at eliminating terrorism.

Finally, acting on recommendations from the Ministry of Finance, the cabinet approved designs for a new series of currency notes alongside a new Rs10 coin to replace the existing banknote. The updated currency features advanced materials and security features to enhance durability and prevent counterfeiting. The cabinet also endorsed prior decisions made by committees regarding state-owned enterprises and legislative cases.

stories.title: Indian Rupee Set to Rally as US Midterms Pressure Oil Prices
stories.summary:
The Indian rupee is expected to strengthen following a drop in global oil prices, triggered by political outcomes in the United States. According to currency traders in Mumbai, the rupee was anticipated to open in the 94.35 to 94.40 range after closing at 94.64 against the US dollar.

International benchmark Brent crude tumbled roughly 8.5 percent to well below $100 per barrel, resting at $94.20 in Asia, which marks a near 20 percent decline for the week. This sharp contraction stems from the US midterm elections, where President Donald Trump’s Republican Party lost control of Congress. Analysts at ING Bank noted that the Democratic Party's victory provides confidence to challenge Trump’s policies regarding Iran, support for Israel, and tariff escalations.

MUFG Bank indicated that the election results signify a shift in the political landscape, unwinding geopolitical risk premiums that had accumulated over eight months of conflict with Iran. Persistent military escalations and uncertainties around the Strait of Hormuz had previously driven up crude valuations as investors priced in prolonged disruptions.

A sustained reduction in oil prices is expected to alleviate direct pressures on the rupee by decreasing India's dollar requirements for energy imports. Furthermore, it aims to enhance the nation's growth and inflation outlook, potentially boosting foreign portfolio investments in Indian assets. Traders emphasize that a continued correction in crude is vital for sustaining the currency's recovery.

stories.title: Global Oil Prices Slide for Fourth Day on US Midterm Fallout
stories.summary:
Oil prices declined for a fourth consecutive session as markets reacted to US midterm election results that are perceived to diminish the likelihood of an escalation in the US-Israeli conflict with Iran. In early trading, Brent futures dropped 97 cents, or 1.03 percent, to $93.65 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude fell $1.14, or 1.29 percent, to $86.98. Both benchmarks had previously tumbled over eight percent to reach their lowest levels since August 31.

Sources close to Gulf government circles suggest that a weakened President Donald Trump, facing a Democratic-controlled Congress capable of limiting military options, holds a greater incentive to pursue a diplomatic resolution. Such a settlement could facilitate the full restoration of Middle Eastern oil flows. June Goh, a senior oil analyst at Sparta Commodities, noted that markets are pricing in a higher probability of the conflict ending, though future volatility remains due to uncertainties surrounding full diplomacy and depleted global strategic reserves.

According to analysts, crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have rebounded close to pre-war levels, albeit at higher costs. JPMorgan reported that this supply recovery returned the global market to a surplus of 1.1 million barrels per day in September, widening to 1.4 million barrels per day in October. Conversely, experts like XAnalysts CEO Mukesh Sahdev caution that the selloff may be temporary, citing low commercial inventories in major consuming nations, upcoming congressional transition timelines, and strong recent demand reported by the Energy Information Administration.

stories.title: US Democrats Win Congress in Midterm Blowout Amid Iran War Backlash
stories.summary:
President Donald Trump’s Republican Party suffered a major electoral defeat in the US midterm elections, as Democrats secured control of both houses of Congress. The outcome reflects widespread domestic dissatisfaction with toxic domestic politics, cost-of-living crises, and the ongoing military conflict with Iran. President Trump himself acknowledged that voter sentiment regarding Iran contributed to the electoral setback.

The international community is closely watching to see if Washington will alter its foreign policy trajectory following the vote. During his second term, Trump disrupted traditional international alliances and partnered with Israel in a conflict against Iran. Just prior to the midterms, Trump announced the termination of a multibillion-dollar aid program to Israel, a move interpreted by observers as an attempt to appease domestic voters increasingly critical of unconditional foreign support.

Despite the legislative shift, expectations for a radical foreign policy transformation may be premature. While a Democratic-led Congress possesses greater oversight capabilities to restrict foreign war funding, the president retains veto authority to override legislative checks. Consequently, political opponents of foreign military intervention must mount concerted efforts to halt strikes on Iran and stop taxpayer funding of campaigns against Palestinians.

As the political landscape shifts, analysts suggest that President Trump may heed the message sent by American voters. Observers argue that the administration should pivot from foreign military engagements toward domestic unity and economic reconstruction.

stories.title: Former Minister Warns Freedom of Navigation Faces Global Threats
stories.summary:
Former Federal Minister Khurram Dastgir Khan stated that the United States' withdrawal from its traditional global role represents a critical shift in the international order, putting the freedom of navigation essential for maritime trade at risk. He made these remarks during a session titled 'Shifting Geopolitics: Risks, Resilience and Prosperity' at the 29th Sustainable Development Conference organized by the Sustainable Development Policy Institute in Islamabad.

Highlighting potential choke points, Dastgir warned that security vulnerabilities could spread from the Strait of Hormuz to the Bab el-Mandeb, Suez Canal, or Panama Canal. He also emphasized that changes in US leadership could alter Washington's diplomatic approach toward Islamabad, necessitating a greater focus on energy diversification and western border engagement for Pakistan. SDPI Executive Director Dr Abid Qaiyum Suleri underscored Pakistan's precarious position amid ongoing geopolitical conflicts.

Other speakers, including Pakistan Regional Economic Forum Chairman Haroon Sharif and former Ambassador to Iran Riffat Masood, discussed global economic uncertainty, the changing nature of state intervention, and regional stability. Masood pointed out that Pakistan has historically neglected its western borders with Iran and Afghanistan, while Maj-Gen Dr Ehsan Mehmood Khan (Retd) noted that major powers continue to rely on war economies.

In separate sessions at the conference, lawmakers and development experts addressed Pakistan's domestic energy challenges, calling for an accelerated transition to utility-scale renewable energy. Participants including MNA Dr Nafisa Shah, MNA Riaz Fatyana, and MNA Barrister Danyal Chaudhry criticized existing power purchase agreements, highlighted the economic necessity of renewables, and urged the restoration of the solar net-metering system to alleviate public unrest.

stories.title: Pakistan Secures Saudi Loan Rollover Amid Waning US Facility Prospects
stories.summary:
Pakistan has obtained a three-month financing rollover from Saudi Arabia as expectations for a proposed $10 billion United States backstop facility diminish. Speaking at Parliament House in Islamabad, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb confirmed that Riyadh extended the $3 billion loan originally provided in April to help cover $3.5 billion in repayments to the United Arab Emirates. The minister noted that the extension covers a reasonable period given the strategic bilateral relationship, following a positive meeting with his Saudi counterpart, Mohammed Al-Jadaan, during the World Bank-IMF meetings in Bangkok. Saudi Arabia had previously extended a separate $5 billion facility until 2028.

Addressing the status of the $10 billion Exchange Stabilisation Support Facility requested from the United States in July, Aurangzeb moderated earlier expectations. He explained that the initial goal was to secure market access, which Pakistan achieved through a recent $3 billion bond issuance that attracted $6 billion in orders. While describing the US facility as a useful potential liquidity support, he emphasized that the country has alternative plans involving Eurobonds, Panda bonds, and rupee-linked dollar-settled issuances. He added that the government intends to engage the US through broader avenues, such as backing from the US Export-Import Bank and the Development Finance Corporation for local investors and exporters. Furthermore, an IMF Executive Board meeting is scheduled for December to approve a $1.2 billion disbursement.

During a briefing to the Senate Standing Committee on Finance, Aurangzeb reported that the government aims to cut external debt by $4 billion during the current fiscal year and $3.5 billion in the following year. By utilizing bond issuances and private placements to replace expensive short-term loans, officials hope to mitigate refinancing risks. Finance Secretary Imdadullah Bosal informed the committee that public debt declined to 68.6% of GDP by the end of June 2026, down from 75.1% in fiscal year 2022-23. Total foreign exchange reserves surpassed $21.5 billion, marking a historic high for the country despite regional conflicts and domestic floods.

The committee also addressed administrative hurdles faced by parliamentarians attempting to acquire foreign exchange for personal travel. Chairman Senator Saleem Mandviwalla criticized the mandatory personal appearances and clearance requirements for politically exposed persons enforced by the State Bank of Pakistan and commercial banks. The committee demanded an immediate review of these procedures and expressed strong dissatisfaction with the central bank's initial response to parliamentary inquiries.

stories.title: PIQ Initiative Expands Robotics and STEM Education Across Pakistan
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Innovation Quest (PIQ) is broadening access to robotics and STEM education for young people nationwide who have traditionally faced barriers due to cost, geography, gender, or disability. Implemented by the Pi Space Science Education Centre (PSSEC) in partnership with the World Robot Olympiad (WRO) Association and powered by Aramco, the national initiative seeks to engage 10,000 learners and 300 teachers through regional competitions, a National Showcase, and over 60 RoboStarter Sprints.

Aramco's sponsorship allows the program to deliver free training across public and private schools, low-income neighborhoods, girls' schools, and NGO-supported entities. A notable inclusion effort took place at the Deaf Reach School, where deaf students utilized robotics kits directly with the aid of sign language interpreters and fluent trainers. According to Zartaj Ahmed, CEO and Co-Founder of PSSEC and National Organizer of WRO Pakistan, the initiative aims to bridge the access divide for those who have never held a robotics kit or imagined themselves as engineers.

The curriculum merges practical robotics instruction with the WRO Future Innovators project cycle to help students earn WRO certification while providing professional development for teachers. The movement has already interacted with more than 6,000 learners and 518 teachers across 60 institutions in Karachi, Lahore, Hyderabad, Gujranwala, and Kasur. PIQ is targeting a female participation rate of over 40 percent and plans to donate 100 robotics kits to underserved institutions.

Hussain N. Hanbazazah, Aramco Vice President of Communications Operations & Corporate Citizenship, noted that the corporation regards STEM education as a vital investment in future innovators and leaders. The initiative provides a structured progression for students, starting from initial hands-on experiences to creating original solutions for real-world problems and competing at regional levels toward the World Robot Olympiad Pakistan platform.

stories.title: Taunsa Farmers Face Severe Water Shortages Amid Chashma Canal Closure
stories.summary:
Farmers in the Taunsa region have been severely impacted by the ongoing closure of the Chashma Right Bank Canal, alongside persistent water theft and insufficient maintenance. The crisis escalated significantly following a structural breach along the inter-provincial waterway, prompting the Water and Power Development Authority to halt water releases from the Chashma Barrage on the Indus River. According to a Punjab Irrigation Department official, the command area suffered massive water deficits during the Kharif season, registering shortages of 77 percent in April, 78 percent in May, 95 percent in June, 98 percent in July, and 96 percent in August.

The situation worsened in September when a major breach occurred in the Paharpur tehsil area located in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, resulting in a complete halt to water flow. The inter-provincial gravity irrigation network spans approximately 606,000 acres, with 240,000 acres—representing about 97,125 hectares—situated in Punjab. The total length of the main canal reaches roughly 274 kilometers, which includes a 103-kilometer section within Punjab that receives supplies at RD-513. The system operates with a head design discharge of about 4,825 cusecs, while Punjab holds a design capacity of 1,834 cusecs and an operational daily indent of 1,800 cusecs, distributed through 30 distributaries and 32 minors totaling nearly 440 kilometers.

Because groundwater across most of the Punjab command area is brackish and unsuitable for agricultural use, the complete supply disruption has severely disrupted scheduled irrigation practices. Officials noted that illegal water extraction and theft by individuals in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa—amounting to an estimated 1,000 cusecs—further aggravated the supply deficits. The main canal was originally constructed by Wapda between 1998 and 2002 as a perennial system. While certain distributaries were transferred to the Punjab Irrigation Department in May 2002, the Punjab section of the main canal and its structures were later handed over following a Council of Common Interests decision in August 2020 and a bilateral agreement in March 2022, though Wapda maintains operational control over the upper segment.

Following the breach on September 14, 2026, head supplies were suspended for two days, and discharges at the Punjab border remained at zero from September 17 to September 30. Wapda subsequently awarded emergency repair and concrete lining contracts worth approximately 385 million rupees on September 30, 2026, with the restoration work expected to take around 45 days. Until these repairs are fully completed and normal operations resume, agricultural lands in Punjab will remain deprived of essential water supplies, raising the risk of significant production losses and crop damage.

stories.title: Trump Adopts Conciliatory Tone After Sweeping Midterm Losses
stories.summary:
US President Donald Trump adopted a surprisingly conciliatory tone following a Democratic sweep in the midterm elections that reduced his administration to lame-duck status. While Trump congratulated the Democrats and expressed a willingness to collaborate, he also shared an image of a red baseball cap featuring the word "VETO," signaling potential legislative gridlock in his remaining two years in office.

Political analysts question how long this cooperative stance will endure, especially as the 80-year-old president retains significant executive and foreign policy powers. The administration has reportedly prepared executive orders to advance hardline immigration policies, mirroring strategies used during the first 100 days of his second term. Foreign policy remains an area of broad unilateral authority for a lame-duck president, raising questions about whether he might resume large-scale military operations against Iran.

Despite the electoral defeat and ongoing fallout from the Iran conflict, Trump signaled that he continues to seek a diplomatic resolution to the war he initiated in February. Ryan Hass of the Brookings Institution noted that Trump likely wants his legacy to reflect a desire for a stronger America rather than being remembered as a warmonger. Furthermore, Trump dismissed speculation that he would remove Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth as part of a cabinet reshuffle.

Trump has long sought to position himself as a peacemaker and is expected to continue pressing Ukraine to agree to a settlement with Russia, with fresh trilateral negotiations scheduled for the following week. However, his political leverage with global leaders such as Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin could potentially be diminished by the domestic setback of the midterm elections.

The midterm results have altered the domestic political landscape, forcing the administration to navigate a newly empowered Democratic opposition in Congress. Whether Trump will maintain a moderate approach or resort to aggressive executive actions remains uncertain as Republicans assess the political cost of the ongoing conflicts.

stories.title: US Federal Judge Blocks Trump Administration Deportation Plan for Afghans
stories.summary:
A federal court in the United States intervened on Tuesday to halt the Trump administration's initiative to expel scores of Afghan immigrants back to Afghanistan. Judge Valerie Caproni of the US District Court for the Southern District of New York issued a ruling preventing the federal government from transferring any Afghan nationals to Afghanistan or Pakistan during the week. The legal action addresses concerns raised by advocacy organizations who argued that sending these individuals back could put their lives in grave danger.

Reports from US media indicated that over 150 Afghans living in the United States were scheduled for removal via Pakistan as part of President Donald Trump's ongoing immigration crackdown. The targeted group reportedly included family members of individuals who had assisted the US military prior to the fall of Kabul. AfghanEvac, a coalition dedicated to supporting former Afghan allies, spearheaded efforts alongside veterans, lawmakers, and thousands of citizens to halt the scheduled transport.

During court proceedings, US Immigration and Customs Enforcement Deputy Assistant Director Christopher George submitted that no chartered or commercial removal flights to Afghanistan or Pakistan were planned or confirmed for the week. Shawn VanDiver, president of AfghanEvac, credited the swift coalition advocacy and congressional pressure for stopping the flight. Meanwhile, Taliban authorities in Afghanistan expressed serious concern earlier over the reported expulsion plans.

The case highlights ongoing international anxiety regarding the safety of former Western allies. While the Taliban administration announced a general amnesty for Afghans who collaborated with foreign forces after seizing power in 2021 and reiterated safety guarantees this year, the United Nations has continued to document instances of extrajudicial killings, arbitrary detentions, and other abuses against returnees.

stories.title: New Delhi Air Pollution Surges to Hazardous Levels Before Diwali Festival
stories.summary:
Toxic air pollution levels in India's capital, New Delhi, spiked dramatically on Wednesday, exceeding the World Health Organization's daily recommended threshold by more than 30 times. Data gathered by air quality monitors showed the severe deterioration occurring just three days after local authorities implemented stricter controls, which included limits on vehicular traffic and construction activities, to combat smog in the metropolitan area of over 30 million residents.

Environmental conditions are projected to deteriorate further ahead of the upcoming Sunday Diwali festival. Although the Supreme Court granted permission for limited use of lower-emission green firecrackers during the celebrations, restrictions are frequently ignored, resulting in widespread explosive displays that compound the poisonous atmosphere. Monitoring firm IQAir recorded PM2.5 concentrations exceeding 461 micrograms per cubic metre in certain sections of the city on Wednesday.

According to figures from India's environment ministry, vehicles are responsible for 23 percent of winter pollution in Delhi, while biomass burning and farm stubble fires account for 20 percent. Industrial sources, including coal-fired power plants, contribute approximately nine percent of the total emissions affecting the region.

The largest share of pollution, estimated at 27 percent, stems from secondary particulate matter created when gases emitted by vehicles, industry, and biomass burning react in the atmosphere. Jacob Koshy, science editor and author of 'The Nitrogen Bomb', notes that this chemical reaction is significantly amplified by massive fertilizer use on surrounding agricultural fields, as released ammonia forms a chemical base layer that accelerates particulate creation.

stories.title: Bangladesh Garment Wage Board Agrees to Higher Pay Amid Ongoing Protests
stories.summary:
Wage board representatives in Bangladesh reached an agreement on Wednesday to increase the minimum compensation for workers in the country's vital garment export sector. However, specific financial details of the settlement remained unavailable immediately, leaving uncertainty over whether the decision would successfully conclude five days of intense labor unrest and violent clashes.

Earlier on Wednesday, tens of thousands of apparel workers staged marches through major industrial districts to demand higher pay scales. Demonstrations turned volatile as participants threw bricks, set police vehicles ablaze, and constructed street barricades, prompting security forces to deploy tear gas to disperse the crowds. Although protests subsided later in the afternoon following the wage board announcement, workers did not instantly return to factory floors to resume manufacturing operations.

Labor leaders reported that many employees remained confused about the specifics of the new agreement. Kamrul Hasan, a representative of the Ekota Garments Sramik Federation, stated that most workers were unfamiliar with the operational procedures of the wage board and were actively utilizing social media to determine if their wages had actually been raised.

Mahmudul Hasan, president of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association, urged employees to head back to their jobs. He emphasized that the labor unrest should diminish given the visible progress achieved by the wage board's decision to adjust the minimum pay structure.

stories.title: Pakistan Exports to Europe Decline During First Quarter Despite GSP+ Status
stories.summary:
Pakistan experienced a decline in export revenues from major Western and Eastern European markets during the first quarter of the 2026-27 fiscal year, despite retaining Generalised Scheme of Preferences status. Overall shipments to Europe contracted slightly during the July-September period, sparking deep concern among economic policymakers even though southern and northern European sectors showed modest growth.

Data compiled by the State Bank of Pakistan indicated that total exports to European nations dropped by 1.84 percent, falling to $2.350 billion in the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 compared to $2.394 billion during the same timeframe the previous year. Analysts attribute the downturn partly to ongoing conflicts in the Middle East and the European Union's preferential trade access granted to India, a primary competitor in the global textile market. Rising energy costs resulting from regional conflicts are expected to further depress consumer demand in Europe.

Regional breakdowns reveal varied performance across the continent. Exports to northern Europe expanded by 21.07 percent to $236.321 million, while southern European trade grew by 5.26 percent to $879.896 million, largely driven by a 17.78 percent increase in shipments to Spain. Conversely, exports to eastern Europe fell by 15.05 percent to $168.761 million.

Western Europe, which represents the largest share of Pakistan's EU exports including major economies like Germany and the Netherlands, saw a contraction of 8.51 percent to $1.065 billion. Meanwhile, shipments to the United Kingdom rose by 6.64 percent to $612.305 million following the post-Brexit transition.

stories.title: Lahore High Court Restricts FIA from Investigating Wilful Loan Defaults
stories.summary:
The Lahore High Court has ruled that the Federal Investigation Agency cannot prosecute bank customers for wilful default unless a banking court first establishes the allegation through civil proceedings. A division bench consisting of Justice Jawad Hassan and Justice Abid Hussain Chattha delivered the verdict while accepting petitions filed by Qaiser Shabbir and other individuals. The petitioners had challenged notices issued by the investigative body under Section 20(7) of the Financial Institutions Recovery of Finances Ordinance 2001 after financial institutions initiated recovery lawsuits against them.

Legal representatives for the petitioners argued that civil and criminal remedies under the ordinance are closely intertwined. They contended that a customer cannot be classified as a wilful defaulter until breach of obligations is conclusively determined by both banking and appellate courts. Conversely, lawyers representing the respondents maintained that each aspect of the offense is independent, asserting that the agency possesses exclusive jurisdiction under Rule 5 of the Rules 2018 and that the challenged notices merely asked for information.

In the judgment authored by Justice Chattha, the court dismissed objections regarding the maintainability of the petitions. The bench explained that while notices issued under Section 160 of the Criminal Procedure Code are typically not open to challenge, judicial review remains permissible if they are issued without jurisdiction, with bad faith, or against the parent statute. The court emphasized that a recovery suit only establishes the payable amount rather than proving a wilful default, which carries both civil and criminal dimensions.

Furthermore, the bench disagreed with a 2019 ruling by a larger Lahore High Court bench that suggested specific sections of the ordinance required no prior civil determination. The judges cautioned that allowing criminal proceedings to start without prior civil findings would grant financial institutions an unregulated, coercive tool to recover undetermined sums through arrests and First Information Reports. The court clarified that the agency's authority stems from the ordinance and the 2018 Rules rather than the Federal Investigation Agency Act.

stories.title: Swat Watershed Faces Over 5°C Warming by Century's End
stories.summary:
A glacier risk assessment focusing on the Swat watershed indicates that the basin will experience temperature increases exceeding 5°C by the end of the century, with the most pronounced warming occurring between October and June. While winter precipitation is projected to remain relatively stable, summer rainfall could more than double under certain climate projections. Conducted by the Green Climate Fund (GCF) with backing from the Asian Development Bank (ADB), the study warns that these shifts will escalate risks of severe flooding, erosion, and infrastructure failure in the region.

The Swat basin, home to more than 10,000 glaciers, is expected to experience a temporary rise in water availability driven by accelerated glacier melt and runoff, which will eventually give way to long-term water deficits as glaciers recede. The evaluation is part of a broader GCF initiative under the 'Glacier to Farms' (G2F) program, which also analyzed pilot watersheds in the Kura, Naryn, and Pyanj basins. These four regions were strategically selected to represent nine developing member countries and guide future expansions across Central and West Asia.

Researchers analyzed four decades of weather records to calibrate global climate models and produce localized projections for the years 2035, 2055, 2085, and 2100. Across the G2F basins, temperatures are expected to climb by 3°C to 5°C, accelerating the degradation of snow, glaciers, and permafrost. These changes will shift seasonal water availability, causing earlier snowmelt and river flow peaks while heightening summer drought risks and agricultural losses.

The melting of glaciers and permafrost leads to slope instability and natural dam degradation, raising the threat of rockfalls, ice avalanches, and glacial lake outburst floods (Glofs). Furthermore, heavy precipitation coupled with rapid spring melting is likely to trigger flash floods and debris flows. Although these hazards present serious threats to human settlements and infrastructure, the assessment concludes that appropriate resilience measures can reduce such risks to manageable levels.

stories.title: Pakistan and UK Express Shared Concern Over Afghan-Based Terrorism
stories.summary:
Pakistan and the United Kingdom held their annual bilateral Counterterrorism Dialogue in Islamabad on Wednesday, voicing serious worries regarding the ongoing threat of terrorist groups, including the TTP, operating inside and from Afghanistan. Both nations emphasized that a stable and secure Afghanistan is essential for achieving enduring peace and regional prosperity. Dr Fareha Bugti, Director General (CT), led the Pakistani delegation, while Thomas Barry, Director for National and Economic Security in the FCDO, headed the UK side.

During the meetings, the UK delegation offered condolences for lives lost in terrorist incidents across Pakistan and reaffirmed its solidarity with Islamabad in counterterrorism efforts. The two delegations engaged in detailed discussions concerning the regional and global security landscape, reviewing threats posed by transnational terrorist networks. They also evaluated existing bilateral and multilateral counterterrorism cooperation, reiterating a mutual dedication to eradicating terrorism in all its forms.

The talks addressed modern challenges in security, including misinformation campaigns, the manipulation of social media platforms, and the misuse of emerging technologies, with both sides exchanging best practices to counter these trends. British officials acknowledged Pakistan's vital contributions to regional stability and security. The participants agreed to deepen institutional ties and maintain continuous communication to further their shared counterterrorism objectives.

At the conclusion of the dialogue, both governments agreed to convene the next round of talks in London in 2027 on mutually agreed dates. The annual engagement underscores the ongoing diplomatic and security cooperation between Islamabad and London in addressing complex transnational threats.

stories.title: Punjab ACS Directs Officials to Support the Business Community
stories.summary:
Additional Chief Secretary Punjab Iftikhar Ali Sahoo has instructed all additional deputy commissioners (ADCs) headquarters to actively assist entrepreneurs and resolve their difficulties. Speaking at a two-day workshop on Economic Development and Business Facilitation at the Civil Secretariat, Sahoo stated that ADCs Headquarters are assigned dedicated responsibilities for business facilitation for the first time, functioning as designated help desks.

The workshop gathered domestic and international investors alongside representatives from various government sectors to discuss entrepreneurial hurdles and foster a more business-friendly environment. Sahoo emphasized that prompt issue resolution and effective complaint redressal must remain paramount, while stressing that economic activity sustains the livelihoods of numerous families by bridging gaps between the government and the private sector.

Secretary Implementation and Coordination Dr Nasir Mahmood Bashir noted that the event aimed to bolster district-level economic operations and enhance collaboration with the private sector. He mentioned that ongoing efforts focus on modernizing and increasing the transparency of the inspection system to better support business functions.

During the sessions, heads of the Excise, Labour, Environment, Food, and Punjab Revenue Authority departments delivered detailed presentations covering their respective enforcement protocols and operational challenges. Sahoo urged all related departments to maintain robust cooperation and coordination with ADCs Headquarters to maximize service delivery and cultivate healthy competition among government institutions.

stories.title: شام اور سعودی عرب کے درمیان دفاعی تعاون اور قرضوں کے معاہدے طے پا گئے
stories.summary:
شام اور سعودی عرب نے دوطرفہ تعلقات کو مزید مستحکم کرنے اور خطے میں سکیورٹی کا تعاون بڑھانے کی غرض سے ایک دفاعی معاہدے پر دستخط کر دیے ہیں۔ یہ اہم معاہدے شامی صدر احمد الشرع کے دورۂ ریاض کے موقع پر طے پائے، جہاں انہوں نے سعودی ولی عہد اور وزیراعظم شہزادہ محمد بن سلمان سے ملاقات کی اور باہمی دلچسپی کے امور پر تبادلہ خیال کیا۔

اس دورے کے دوران سعودی عرب نے شام میں تعمیرِ نو، توانائی، صحت، رہائش اور بنیادی ڈھانچے کے مختلف منصوبوں کے لیے 403 ملین ڈالر سے زائد کے رعایتی قرضے فراہم کرنے پر بھی اتفاق کیا۔ شامی وزارتِ خارجہ نے دونوں ممالک کی وزارتِ دفاع کے درمیان ہونے والے اس معاہدے کو اس دورے کی سب سے بڑی کامیابیوں میں سے ایک قرار دیا ہے۔

تاہم، فریقین کی جانب سے اس دفاعی معاہدے کی تکنیکی تفصیلات، سکیورٹی تعاون کی نوعیت اور اس پر عمل درآمد کے طریقہ کار کو تاحال منظرِ عام پر نہیں لایا گیا ہے۔ شامی وزارت خارجہ نے اسے دونوں ممالک کے تعلقات میں ایک نیا سنگِ میل اور خطے میں تعاون کی فضا کو فروغ دینے والا قدم بتایا ہے۔

یہ معاہدہ ایسے وقت میں سامنے آیا ہے جب سعودی عرب کو یمن میں حوثی باغیوں کی جانب سے کیے جانے والے میزائل اور ڈرون حملوں کا سامنا ہے، اور وہ خطے سمیت دنیا بھر کے مختلف ممالک کے ساتھ مل کر اپنی دفاعی صلاحیتوں کو مزید مؤثر بنانے کی کوششوں میں مصروف ہے۔

stories.title: Global Oil Prices Drop Over Eight Percent Following US Midterm Elections
stories.summary:
Crude oil prices tumbled by more than 8 percent to touch their lowest settlement points in over two months following the US midterm elections. Brent futures decreased by USD8.98, or 8.7 percent, to settle at USD94.62 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate crude dropped by USD7.97, or 8.3 percent, to USD88.12 a barrel. Both primary benchmarks reached their weakest levels since August 31.

The market sell-off was triggered by President Donald Trump's Republican Party losing control of Congress, which investors believe could compel a quicker resolution to the US-Israeli war with Iran. Dennis Kissler of BOK Financial noted that Democratic control over Congress could restrict Middle Eastern military spending and increase the probability of an earlier peace accord, compounding downward pressure alongside growing regional crude exports.

President Trump acknowledged that the conflict influenced the midterm election results, which delivered control of the House of Representatives and the Senate to Democrats. Meanwhile, Vice President JD Vance blamed the war entirely for the electoral setback. Gulf exports of crude, condensate, and refined products averaged 17.1 million barrels per day in October, down from 18.9 million barrels per day in September.

Domestically, the US Energy Information Administration reported that national crude inventories decreased by 865,000 barrels to 409.8 million barrels during the week ending October 30. Despite hopes for de-escalation, some analysts caution that a negotiated agreement remains distant and that political shifts could potentially provoke further volatility rather than immediate stability.

stories.title: Pakistan LNG Limited Invites Bids for Two Winter Cargoes
stories.summary:
Pakistan LNG Limited (PLL) has announced an international tender to acquire two liquefied natural gas cargoes for delivery to Port Qasim in Karachi. Identified as tender number PLL/IMP/LNGT80, the procurement aims to satisfy national gas demand during the upcoming winter season by securing deliveries on a Delivered Ex-Ship basis.

The specified delivery windows cover December 14-16, 2026, for the first cargo, and January 9-11, 2027, for the second cargo. Each required shipment carries a volume specification of 140,000 cubic metres, allowing for a tolerance margin of plus or minus five percent in accordance with official bidding guidelines.

Electronic bids must be submitted through version 2.0 of the E-Pak Acquisition and Disposal System (EPADS) by November 6, 2026, at 2:00 pm, with public opening scheduled for 2:30 pm on the same day. The state-owned enterprise stressed that manual submissions will not be accepted, and unregistered international suppliers must complete their enrollment via the EPADS vendor portal to participate.

As a government-mandated entity, PLL continually arranges imported gas supplies to support domestic energy requirements and maintain stability within the local market. This latest tender highlights ongoing efforts to secure essential fuel inventories ahead of peak consumption periods.

stories.title: FBR Data Reveals Millions File Tax Returns Solely for Asset Deals
stories.summary:
Data from the Federal Board of Revenue indicates that nearly 12 million income tax return filers submit documentation exclusively to execute one-time financial deals involving vehicles or immovable property. According to sources, the tax authority’s system regularly dispatches notices to these registered individuals.

Out of the roughly 12 million registered through single transactions, only about 7.5 million maintain continuous filing habits. Because these notices operate digitally via email, non-compliance typically becomes apparent only when a stop-filer attempts to access their IRIS account to process a new transactional filing.

Industry sources suggest that authorities may need to clean up the system by eliminating mandatory filing prerequisites for non-income earners. The FBR previously attempted to address this in the Finance Act 2025 by proposing restrictions on economic transactions, though those measures were ultimately limited by broader economic and political constraints.

once such restrictions are successfully implemented, the submission of returns by spouses and dependent children strictly for isolated asset purchases is expected to cease. Meanwhile, the FBR continues to enforce compliance, recently marking thousands of taxpayers as inactive following the missed October 31 filing deadline.

stories.title: Pakistan and Mastercard Discuss Digital Payments and Financial Inclusion Cooperation
stories.summary:
Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb recently met with a Mastercard delegation headed by Mark Elliott, Division President for East Arabia. The discussion focused on expanding cooperation in digital payments, cybersecurity, and financial inclusion to support Pakistan's transition toward a cashless economy. Officials attending the meeting included Arslan Khan, Country Manager for Pakistan and Afghanistan, alongside Jibran Jamshad, Director of Public Sector for the same region.

During the talks, Senator Aurangzeb praised Mastercard's long-term involvement in Pakistan's financial sector. He emphasized the government's objective to broaden financial service access and improve transparency. The Prime Minister's cashless economy initiative was highlighted as a key driver for utilizing digital tools to assist small and medium enterprises, agriculture, and other underserved groups.

Additional topics included upgrading cross-border remittances, fortifying digital payment infrastructure, and prioritizing cybersecurity. The Finance Minister noted that robust fraud prevention is vital for building a secure digital financial ecosystem. He welcomed Mastercard's ongoing investments and underscored the government's dedication to public-private partnerships.

Mark Elliott reaffirmed Mastercard's commitment to Pakistan, offering the company's global technological expertise to aid the nation's digital transformation. Both parties agreed to maintain close contact and pursue practical avenues of collaboration to bolster Pakistan's digital economy.

stories.title: مولانا فضل الرحمان کے اہل خانہ اور قریبی ساتھیوں کیخلاف ٹیکس چوری کی درخواست
stories.summary:
پاکستان کے سیاسی منظر نامے میں ایک اہم پیش رفت کے تحت جمعیت علمائے اسلام (جے یو آئی) کے سربراہ مولانا فضل الرحمان کے اہل خانہ اور قریبی ساتھیوں کے خلاف مبینہ ٹیکس چوری اور آمدن چھپانے کی شکایت فیڈرل بورڈ آف ریونیو (ایف بی آر) میں جمع کرا دی گئی ہے۔ اس درخواست کا مقصد نامزد شخصیات کی مالی بے ضابطگیوں کی تحقیقات کرنا ہے۔

ایف بی آر میں جمع کروائی گئی اس شکایت میں جن نمایاں افراد کو نامزد کیا گیا ہے ان میں سینیٹر کامران مرتضیٰ، لطف الرحمان، ضیاء الرحمان، اسعد محمود اور ابرار احمد خان شامل ہیں۔ شکایت گزار کی جانب سے ان تمام افراد کے اثاثوں، بینک اکاؤنٹس اور ذرائع آمدن کی گہرائی سے جانچ پڑتال کا مطالبہ کیا گیا ہے۔

درخواست میں سینیٹر کامران مرتضیٰ کے ملکی و غیر ملکی کرنسی اکاؤنٹس، لطف الرحمان اور اسعد محمود کی کاروباری سرگرمیوں، ضیاء الرحمان کے اکاؤنٹس میں موجود غیر واضح رقوم، اور ابرار احمد خان کے ٹریول اینڈ ٹورز کے کاروبار کی مالی ٹرانزیکشنز کا تقابلی جائزہ لینے کی استدعا کی گئی ہے۔ اس کے علاوہ مختلف فلاحی، تعلیمی اور کاروباری اداروں سے ہونے والے مالی لین دین کی چھان بین کا بھی کہا گیا ہے۔

یہ شکایت نامزد سیاسی شخصیات کے اثاثوں اور ٹیکس گوشواروں کے بارے میں غیر جانبدارانہ تحقیقات اور قانونی کارروائی کا تقاضا کرتی ہے۔ اس پیش رفت سے ملکی سیاسی حلقوں میں ہلچل مچ گئی ہے اور متعلقہ اداروں کی طرف سے اس معاملے پر آئندہ کے اقدامات کا انتظار کیا جا رہا ہے۔

stories.title: World Bank Predicts Decline in Pakistan's Cotton Output Amid Global Pressures
stories.summary:
Pakistan's vital cotton crop faces another projected drop in production, threatening an economy heavily reliant on its primary merchandise export industry. According to World Bank forecasts, domestic cotton output is expected to fall by 6 percent in the 2026-27 period, whereas global output is predicted to decline by 3 percent. Meanwhile, Brazil and India are both anticipated to grow their respective cotton production by about 1 percent each.

This declining domestic yield worsens the textile sector's reliance on imported cotton, raising foreign exchange demands and exposing manufacturers to international price volatility and supply chain disruptions. Compounding these agricultural challenges, international commodity markets face severe headwinds. Conflicts in the Middle East, ongoing disruptions from the Russia-Ukraine war, and a potential El Niño threat are driving up energy and transport costs. The World Bank projects global commodity prices to increase by 23 percent in 2026, accompanied by a 32 percent surge in energy prices and a 10 percent rise in food costs.

Historically, Pakistan held a strong natural advantage in cotton production, supporting millions of jobs across farming, ginning, spinning, weaving, and manufacturing. However, inadequate planning and a lack of coordinated support have allowed this advantage to erode. Policymakers must move beyond short-term fixes and implement a multi-year strategy addressing seed quality, pest management, water availability, and climate-resilient farming varieties.

To safeguard the agricultural foundations of the country's flagship export sector, the government needs to unite provincial administrations, researchers, growers, and textile manufacturers. Establishing clear production targets and predictable support systems will be essential for overcoming successive shortfalls and preventing competitors from capturing market share.

stories.title: Aasaan Tax Scheme Struggles to Attract Traders Amid IMF Pressure
stories.summary:
Pakistan's Aasaan tax scheme has encountered severe difficulties in registering traders, drawing only 222 participants compared to the targeted one million. This follows the similar underperformance of its 2024 predecessor, the Taajir Dost scheme. Both initiatives aimed to expand the tax net, but faced heavy resistance from traders and widespread non-compliance, prompting the Federal Board of Revenue to utilize strict enforcement measures such as utility cut-offs.

The Aasaan scheme features a flat one percent turnover tax on annual sales or a minimum of 25,000 rupees, offering audit exemptions and QR-coded protection against random inspections. In contrast, the earlier Taajir Dost framework utilized monthly advance minimum taxes based on electricity bills and commercial property valuations. Current registration appears largely limited to large shopkeepers with an annual turnover of 200 million rupees or 20 crore rupees, who qualify for withholding tax and point of sale exemptions.

International Monetary Fund documents from May 2026 note that consolidation progress has heavily relied on formal sector revenue. To improve compliance, the Federal Board of Revenue introduced a new audit workflow and hired 431 auditors by March 2026, with another 396 planned by the end of June 2026. Despite these administrative steps, Pakistan's tax-to-GDP ratio dropped to 10.3 percent in the 2025-26 fiscal year, lingering well below regional peers.

Analysts argue that broad revenue administration improvements are necessary to address structural tax distortions and reduce reliance on narrow measures. Exemptions on residential property sales and certain foods continue to cost the economy revenue, while digital invoicing and production monitoring remain limited to specific subsectors like sugar, cement, and fertilizer.

stories.title: Pakistan and China's Xinjiang Explore Investment and Agricultural Joint Ventures
stories.summary:
Delegates from China's Xinjiang Province and Pakistani business leaders recently met at the Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry to identify joint venture opportunities across agriculture, textiles, food processing, livestock, and manufacturing. Chinese delegation leader Ha Zengyou urged entrepreneurs to turn bilateral agreements into practical economic projects, introducing a four-pronged framework focusing on agriculture, textiles, new trade channels, and regional connectivity.

Ha Zengyou noted that Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps and Lahore share complementary industrial strengths. He pointed out that Pakistan possesses strong potential in fruits, vegetables, seafood, berries, and nuts, while Xinjiang can provide expertise in modern farming, livestock, and cold-chain facilities. Furthermore, he proposed closer industrial integration between Pakistan's cotton spinning capabilities and Xinjiang's textile sector.

During the discussions, Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry President Ali Hussam Asghar highlighted promising sectors for collaboration, including water-efficient farming, food packaging, and halal meat production, while inviting Chinese investors to utilize Punjab's industrial estates and CPEC Special Economic Zones. Senior Vice President Sardar Usman Ghani proposed constructing a secure Chinatown in Lahore to host visiting Chinese professionals and business owners.

Additionally, former Chamber President Shahzad Ali Malik emphasized adopting Xinjiang's cotton cultivation and seed development techniques to reverse Pakistan's declining cotton yields, which have fallen from roughly 15 million bales historically to 5-6 million bales. Separately, Ethiopian Ambassador to Pakistan Dr Oumer Hussien Oba visited the chamber to invite Pakistani businesses to explore trade and investment opportunities in Ethiopia's growing economy.

stories.title: Punjab Chief Minister Inaugurates Special Education Centre in Hassan Abdal
stories.summary:
Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif has formally inaugurated the Nawaz Sharif Centre of Excellence for Special Education, marking the establishment of the first such major facility for special children in the Rawalidpindi Division. Located in the remote area of Hassan Abdal, the centre commenced operations with the chief minister arriving hand-in-hand with differently-abled girls.

During her visit, Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz toured the facility to inspect specially designed classrooms catering to children with hearing and speech impairments, as well as observing teaching techniques for those with congenital physical disabilities. She also spent time in the music and activity rooms, where she shared warm interactions with students. Among them, a student named Sawaira sang songs, while another child, Sufyan, humorously asked for the chief minister's WhatsApp number. The participants were deeply moved by Ahmed Ali, a young boy born without arms and legs, whom the chief minister warmly embraced.

Praising the resilience and courage of the children, the chief minister referred to them as superheroes. She also held a separate meeting with a young girl and her mother who had suffered acid burns. The inauguration highlights regional efforts to enhance educational and support infrastructure for differently-abled youth in remote areas.

The initiative matters significantly for local families in Hassan Abdal and surrounding remote regions who previously lacked specialized institutional support for children with special needs. By bringing advanced educational facilities and dedicated care closer to these communities, the centre aims to foster inclusivity and personal growth for vulnerable children.

stories.title: Lahore Chamber Hosts Seminar Focusing on Underprivileged Youth Talent
stories.summary:
The Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) recently hosted a seminar dedicated to the welfare and educational future of underprivileged and talented youth. The event was organized in collaboration with Aspiring Futures USA and brought together prominent figures from business, philanthropy, and government sectors.

Key attendees at the seminar included Chairman of the Chief Minister’s Task Force on Prisons Rana Mannan Khan, defense analyst Babar Alauddin, former LCCI president Mian Abu Zar Shad, and Uzma Qureshi, the founder and president of Aspiring Futures USA. During the discussions, speakers underscored the critical importance of supporting deserving students to secure the nation's future. Babar Alauddin praised the impactful work done by Aspiring Futures, while Rana Mannan Khan promised complete governmental facilitation at administrative levels.

Uzma Qureshi addressed the primary needs of underprivileged youth, stressing that they require proper resources and guidance rather than just financial scholarships. She emphasized that the organization's core objective is to dismantle specific barriers in a child's educational journey, thereby integrating them into the mainstream education system to become self-reliant citizens. LCCI leadership reaffirmed their strong commitment to supporting this welfare mission.

The event concluded with journalist and advisor Haider Munir thanking all distinguished guests for their steadfast support. In recognition of her dedicated services in education and social welfare, the LCCI presented a commemorative shield to Uzma Qureshi, marking a successful collaboration between local business leaders and international philanthropic efforts.

stories.title: Farmers Give Government Ten-Day Deadline Over Sugarcane Support Prices
stories.summary:
Farmers in Pakistan have issued a ten-day ultimatum to the government to declare sugarcane support prices and initiate the annual crushing season, threatening a march toward Islamabad if their demands are ignored. The warning was delivered during a joint press conference at the Karachi Press Club by leaders of the Sindh Abadgar Ittehad and Kisan Ittehad.

Kisan Ittehad President Khalid Hussain Batth criticized the government for failing to issue a notification on sugarcane prices or set a crushing date, causing widespread uncertainty. Growers are demanding a support price of Rs 650 per maund for sugarcane alongside Rs 4,500 per maund for wheat. Batth highlighted ongoing inflation, pointing out that citizens are compelled to buy flour at Rs 190 per kilogram despite the arrival of imported wheat shipments. Sindh Abadgar Ittehad President Nawab Zubair Talpur added that crushing operations should have officially commenced on November 1, noting that surplus stocks of around 1 million tonnes of sugar exist while growers remain unpaid for their produce.

Beyond pricing concerns, agricultural leaders emphasized mounting pressures from water shortages reaching tail-end areas, rising diesel expenses, and high costs for DAP fertilizer. These combined challenges have severely damaged crops and escalated production costs for farmers across the region.

The ongoing dispute directly impacts the country's agricultural backbone and food security. Failure to resolve these grievances risks widespread protests in the capital, severe disruptions to the sugar milling season, and continued financial distress for rural farming communities already grappling with severe resource constraints.

stories.title: Korean Embassy Announces Three-Day K-Festival 2026 in Karachi
stories.summary:
The Karachi Office of the Embassy of the Republic of Korea, alongside the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA), is set to host a three-day economic and cultural event named 'K-Festival 2026' at Lucky Mall in Karachi from November 13 to 15. The festival will showcase South Korean cultural heritage and consumer products by uniting local distributors, businesses, and enthusiasts.

During a media briefing, Korean Consul General Joohoon (Jay) Kim announced that major South Korean brands like Samsung Electronics and Lotte Kolson, alongside 14 local distribution networks, will participate. Nine exhibition booths will feature cosmetics, food items, household goods, electronics, and automotive accessories. Visitors will also experience traditional Korean attire, known as Hanbok, and explore various lifestyle showcases.

A primary highlight of the festival will be a live performance by nuMori, an innovative South Korean music band specializing in 'Electro Gugak'—a genre blending traditional Korean music with rock and K-pop. Additionally, the event will host the 'KTS: Karachi to Seoul' K-Pop Festival on Sunday, featuring nine finalist teams competing in vocal and dance categories for electronic prizes. The band will also perform at the World Culture Festival organized by the Arts Council of Karachi on November 16.

The festival aims to strengthen bilateral cultural exchanges, enhance people-to-people contacts, and provide Karachi residents with an immersive experience of contemporary and traditional Korean lifestyle. It offers a unique platform for youth and culture enthusiasts to engage directly with South Korean commercial and artistic offerings.

stories.title: Virat Kohli's Brilliant 74 Leads India to ODI Victory Over New Zealand
stories.summary:
India secured a five-wicket victory over New Zealand in the opening One-day International at Eden Park in Auckland on Wednesday. Veteran batsman Virat Kohli played a decisive role, scoring 74 runs from 51 deliveries to claim his 80th ODI fifty. The match was affected by rain delays, resulting in a revised target for the touring side.

New Zealand was restricted to 185 all out in the 41st over during the first innings. Tim Seifert top-scored with 38 runs, while Arshdeep Singh claimed four wickets for 70 runs and Gurnoor Brar took three wickets for 44 runs. India's chase was anchored by a 113-run partnership between Kohli and captain Shubman Gill, who contributed 37 runs.

Rain interruptions forced the target to be adjusted to 143 runs in 32 overs under the Duckworth-Lewis method. Kohli attacked New Zealand's bowling attack with 13 fours and a single six before India successfully chased the target with 56 balls remaining, taking a 1-0 lead in the five-match series.

The victory gives India an early advantage in the series ahead of the second match scheduled in Wellington on Saturday. Kohli's performance stood out on a bouncy pitch where other batsmen struggled to find consistency.

stories.title: Top seeds Zverev and Djokovic exit Paris Masters early
stories.summary:
World number one Alexander Zverev and 24-time Grand Slam champion Novak Djokovic both suffered surprise defeats during the round-of-32 matches at the Paris Masters on November 4, 2026. Playing at the Plenitude Arena in Nanterre, on the outskirts of Paris, France, Zverev fell 7-6(7/5), 6-2 to 24th-ranked Lorenzo Musetti. Zverev expressed frustration afterward regarding questions about his top ranking. Meanwhile, Djokovic lost 2-6, 6-3, 6-3 to 83rd-ranked Australian qualifier Rinky Hijikata, a defeat that ends the 39-year-old's campaign and his hopes of qualifying for the ATP Finals.

In contrast, second seed Carlos Alcaraz advanced by defeating American Alex Michelsen 7-6(7/4), 6-3 during the night session. Alcaraz acknowledged the difficult day for top players after avoiding a similar upset. Former world number one Daniil Medvedev also exited in straight sets against Peru's Ignacio Buse, and seventh seed Frances Tiafoe lost to Quentin Halys. Halys' victory secured a spot in the ATP Finals for Frenchman Arthur Fils, who later defeated Tomas Machac.

The tournament outcomes reshaped the draws as players vie for crucial season-ending positions. Zverev's defeat followed his recent major wins at the French and US Opens, which had propelled him to the top of the ATP rankings earlier in November. Djokovic indicated his immediate plan is simply to rest following his elimination.

As the tournament progresses, attention shifts toward the upcoming round of 16 fixtures. Ben Shelton is scheduled to face Arthur Rinderknech, while Carlos Alcaraz prepares to meet Matteo Berrettini in the night session. These matches will determine who advances to the quarter-finals in the French capital.

stories.title: Valverde seals late Real Madrid win as Liverpool fall
stories.summary:
Federico Valverde scored a stoppage-time winner to secure a 3-2 victory for Real Madrid against AEK Athens in the UEFA Champions League on November 4, 2026. Real twice came from behind at Agia Sophia Stadium in Athens, with Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappe also scoring, keeping Real second in the standings with 12 points from four matches behind Paris Saint-Germain on goal difference.

Liverpool experienced a contrasting result in Istanbul, surrendering the lead twice before losing 3-2 to Fenerbahce at Sukru Saracoglu Stadium. Trey Nyoni and Alexander Isak scored for Liverpool, but Fenerbahce responded through Mason Greenwood, an own goal, and a 79th-minute winner by Vedat Muriqi. The defeat dropped Liverpool to eighth place with nine points, while Fenerbahce climbed to 19th with five points.

Elsewhere, Manchester City defeated RB Leipzig 3-2 thanks to a 78th-minute goal by Erling Haaland, placing City seventh with nine points. Arsenal overcame Slavia Prague 2-1 to move into third place with 10 points. Como recorded a historic 9-1 victory against RC Lens in France, matching the competition's record winning margin with a hat-trick from Anastasios Douvikas.

In other matches, FC Porto earned their first points by defeating Napoli 4-1, Borussia Dortmund beat Real Betis 2-1 with a winner from Konstantinos Karetsas, and Club Brugge secured a 2-1 victory over PSV Eindhoven. The results significantly shifted standings across the Champions League table as the group stage matches continued to unfold across Europe.

stories.title: یمنی حوثیوں کا ریاض ایئرپورٹ پر میزائل حملہ، ایران کی سخت انتباہ
stories.summary:
یمنی حوثیوں نے سعودی عرب کے دارالحکومت ریاض میں واقع کنگ خالد انٹرنیشنل ایئرپورٹ پر بیلسٹک میزائل حملے کا دعویٰ کیا ہے۔ اس کے ساتھ ہی، ایرانی وزارتِ خارجہ کے ترجمان اسماعیل بقائی نے خبردار کیا ہے کہ ایران پر دوبارہ ہونے والے کسی بھی حملے کے نتائج ماضی کی نسبت کہیں زیادہ سنگین ہوں گے۔ خطے کی اس بڑھتی ہوئی کشیدگی کے تناظر میں قطری وزیرِاعظم اور وزیرِ خارجہ نے سعودی عرب اور کویت کے وزرائے خارجہ سے الگ الگ ٹیلیفونک رابطے کیے، جن میں علاقائی امن، سلامتی اور کشیدگی میں کمی لانے کے سفارتی اقدامات پر تبادلۂ خیال کیا گیا۔

دوسری جانب، ویانا میں ایرانی وفد نے بین الاقوامی ایٹمی توانائی ایجنسی (آئی اے ای اے) کے ڈائریکٹر جنرل رافیل گروسی کو تنقید کا نشانہ بناتے ہوئے کہا کہ وہ ایران کے جوہری پروگرام پر تشویش کا اظہار تو کرتے ہیں لیکن ایرانی تنصیبات پر ہونے والی غیرقانونی بمباری پر خاموش رہتے ہیں۔ ایرانی وفد نے یاد دلایا کہ جوہری عدم پھیلاؤ کے معاہدے کے تحت یورینیم کی افزودگی کی کوئی مخصوص حد مقرر نہیں ہے۔ اس دوران، بین الاقوامی امدادی تنظیم ریڈ کراس نے اعلان کیا ہے کہ حوثی محاصرے کے آغاز کے بعد پہلی بار چار ٹرکوں پر مشتمل طبی امداد کی کھیپ یمن کے شہر تعز روانہ کر دی گئی ہے تاکہ مقامی ہسپتالوں کی قلت کو دور کیا جا سکے۔

امریکہ کے وسط مدتی انتخابات میں ریپبلکن پارٹی کی شکست اور ڈونلڈ ٹرمپ کے خلاف ردعمل پر ایرانی حکام نے بھی بیانات دیے۔ ایران کی سپریم نیشنل سکیورٹی کونسل کے سیکریٹری محسن رضائی اور ملک کے سپریم لیڈر کے پیغامات میں کہا گیا کہ ایرانی قوم نے میدانِ جنگ اور آبنائے ہرمز میں ٹرمپ کو سٹریٹجک شکست سے دوچار کیا ہے۔ ایرانی حکام نے باور کرایا کہ تہران کے خلاف کسی بھی قسم کی جارحیت کا جواب انتہائی وسیع پیمانے پر دیا جائے گا۔

خطے کے ان تمام جیو سیاسی چیلنجز اور عسکری تناؤ کے درمیان سفارتی کوششیں بھی جاری ہیں تاکہ مشرقِ وسطیٰ کے حالات کو مزید بگڑنے سے روکا جا سکے۔ یمن میں انسانی بحران کے حل کے لیے بین الاقوامی سطح پر طبی امداد کی رسائی کو بحال کرنے کی کوششیں کی جا رہی ہیں، جبکہ دوسری طرف تہران اور واشنگٹن کے مابین لفظی جنگ اور تزویراتی بیانات کا سلسلہ بھی تاحال جاری ہے۔

stories.title: Pakistani Opposition Leaders Form United Alliance to Strengthen Parliament
stories.summary:
Opposition leaders from various political parties gathered in Islamabad on Wednesday at the residence of Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman. The participants, including National Assembly Opposition Leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, agreed to strengthen their alliance and parliamentary coordination. During the meeting, attendees discussed the emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, democratic rights, and plans for a multi-party conference (MPC).

Leaders from the Pakistan Tehreek-Insaf (PTI), JUI-F, and Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) attended the gathering. Achakzai condemned a character assassination campaign against Fazl, while Fazl criticized federal control efforts over coastal belts and islands, and defended the public mandate in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The opposition decided to form committees to resolve internal differences and continue consultations. Meanwhile, PTI representatives raised concerns regarding the health of imprisoned PTI founder Imran Khan, stating his blood pressure had surged and demanding his transfer to Shifa International Hospital.

The meeting followed the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on October 11, which the Centre attributed to security challenges and the provincial government's disengagement from counterterrorism efforts. Opposition figures rejected the move as illegal and accused authorities of violating citizens' privacy through detentions. The gathering highlighted growing political friction as opposition groups coordinate their strategies against the government.

stories.title: امریکہ میں وسط مدتی انتخابات کی شکست کی بڑی وجہ ایران جنگ بنی، جے ڈی وینس
stories.summary:
امریکی نائب صدر جے ڈی وینس نے ایک بیان میں اعتراف کیا ہے کہ ایران کے خلاف جاری جنگ ریپبلکن پارٹی کی وسط مدتی انتخابات میں شکست کی بنیادی وجہ بن گئی ہے۔ انہوں نے سوشل میڈیا پلیٹ فارم ایکس پر اپنے خیالات کا اظہار کرتے ہوئے موجودہ جنگی پالیسی پر بھی سوالات اٹھائے ہیں۔ ان کا کہنا تھا کہ اس جنگ کے نتیجے میں سینیٹ میں اگلے چھ سال کے لیے اکثریت کھونا ایک بڑا نقصان ہے اور اس مؤقف کا دفاع کیا جانا چاہیے۔

اس بیان کے ذریعے جے ڈی وینس کے حوالے سے یہ بھی کہا جا رہا ہے کہ وہ ایران کی جنگ سے سیاسی فاصلہ اختیار کرنے کی کوشش کر رہے ہیں، خاص طور پر اس پس منظر میں کہ انہیں سنہ 2028 کے صدارتی انتخابات کا ممکنہ امیدوار سمجھا جا رہا ہے۔ امریکی انتخابات میں ریپبلکنز کو اس بڑی پسپائی کا سامنا کرنا پڑا ہے، جس سے سیاسی حلقوں میں ہلچل مچ گئی ہے۔

دوسری جانب صدر ڈونلڈ ٹرمپ نے بھی انتخابی نتائج میں ایران جنگ کے کردار کو تسلیم کیا ہے، لیکن انہوں نے اس جنگ کو شروع کرنے کے فیصلے پر کسی قسم کی پشیمانی کا اظہار نہیں کیا۔ صدر ٹرمپ کا موقف ہے کہ انہوں نے بالکل درست قدم اٹھایا تھا اور اگر انہیں دوبارہ موقع ملا تو وہ یہی فیصلہ پھر سے دہرائیں گے۔

یہ صورتحال امریکی سیاسی منظر نامے میں ایک اہم موڑ کی حیثیت رکھتی ہے جہاں حکمران جماعت کو اہم انتخابی نقصان کا سامنا کرنا پڑا ہے۔ عوام اور سیاسی رہنما اس جنگ کے اثرات اور اس کے سیاسی نتائج پر بحث کر رہے ہیں، جس سے مستقبل کے صدارتی انتخابات پر بھی گہرے اثرات مرتب ہو سکتے ہیں۔

stories.title: موجودہ نظام کی بنیادیں شروع سے ہی درست نہیں، راجا ناصر عباس
stories.summary:
سینیٹ میں اپوزیشن لیڈر علامہ راجا ناصر عباس نے ایک بیان میں کہا ہے کہ موجودہ سیاسی نظام جب سے سامنے آیا ہے اس کی ابتدائی بنیاد ہی غلط رکھی گئی ہے۔ انہوں نے مزید بتایا کہ خیبر پختونخوا میں ایمرجنسی نافذ کی گئی اور عوام کو یہ باور کرایا گیا کہ وہ موجودہ مینڈیٹ کو تسلیم نہیں کرتے ہیں۔ 

پاکستان تحریک انصاف کے رہنماؤں کے مطابق بانی پی ٹی آئی کی صحت کو سنگین خطرات لاحق ہیں اور حکومت نے تمام حدود عبور کر لی ہیں۔ ان کا کہنا ہے کہ بانی پی ٹی آئی کا بلڈ پریشر کنٹرول میں نہیں آ رہا جو کہ شدید تشویشناک امر ہے اور اس حوالے سے مسلسل خدشات پائے جاتے ہیں کہ سب کچھ ٹھیک نہیں ہے۔ 

دوسری جانب محمود خان اچکزئی کا کہنا ہے کہ تمام تر ملکی پالیسیاں پارلیمنٹ کے اندر ہی بنائی جانی چاہئیں۔ پی ٹی آئی اور جے یو آئی آئندہ کے لائحہ عمل کے لیے ایک ساتھ بیٹھیں گی اور اے پی سی قومی اتفاق رائے کی جانب ایک اہم قدم ثابت ہو گی۔ 

اس اے پی سی کے انعقاد کے لیے ایک خصوصی کمیٹی تشکیل دی گئی ہے جس میں کامران مرتضیٰ، ناصر شیرازی، سلمان اکرم راجا، عامر ڈوگر اور مصطفیٰ نواز کھوکھر شامل ہیں۔ اس کے علاوہ اخوانزادہ حسین یوسفزئی اور خالد یوسف چودھری اس قومی مشاورتی کانفرنس کے لیے کوآرڈینیٹر کے فرائض انجام دیں گے۔

stories.title: Pulisic and Balogun Return to US Squad for CONCACAF Matches
stories.summary:
Forwards Christian Pulisic and Folarin Balogun have been named in the United States squad for the upcoming CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final matches against Haiti. Head coach Mauricio Pochettino announced the 25-player selection on Wednesday. This marks the first time both players are back in the national team since participating in the World Cup. They had previously missed friendly matches against Peru, Chile, Mexico, and Canada held in September and October.

Pulisic missed those fixtures while recovering from a lower leg bone bruise and a microfracture sustained during the World Cup. He has since resumed playing for his club side, AC Milan. Meanwhile, AS Monaco forward Balogun returns following a turbulent summer. His offseason involved controversy surrounding a FIFA decision to suspend a one-game red-card ban he received at the World Cup, alongside a failed transfer attempt to English club Everton.

The United States squad is currently pursuing its fourth CONCACAF Nations League title. The team will play the first leg against Haiti on November 14 in Miami. Three days later, on November 17, the US will host the Caribbean side for the return leg in Cincinnati.

These upcoming quarter-final encounters are critical for the American team as they look to secure another regional championship. The inclusion of experienced talents like Pulisic and Balogun provides a significant boost to the roster under Pochettino's leadership as they prepare to face Haiti.

stories.title: کراچی میں لیاقت آباد کے قریب مبینہ پولیس مقابلہ، ایک ڈاکو زخمی گرفتار
stories.summary:
شہر قائد کے علاقے لیاقت آباد میں بدھ اور جمعرات کی درمیانی شب بی ایریا اسٹوڈنٹ گراؤنڈ کے قریب پولیس اور ملزمان کے درمیان مبینہ مقابلہ ہوا۔ اس کارروائی کے نتیجے میں ایک ڈاکو زخمی حالت میں گرفتار کر لیا گیا جبکہ اس کا ایک ساتھی موقع سے فرار ہونے میں کامیاب ہو گیا۔

پولیس ترجمان کے مطابق زخمی حالت میں پکڑے جانے والے ملزم کی شناخت شہروز ولد مہتاب حسین کے نام سے ہوئی ہے۔ گرفتاری کے بعد اسے فوری طور پر طبی امداد فراہم کرنے کے لیے عباسی شہید اسپتال منتقل کر دیا گیا جہاں اس کا علاج جاری ہے۔

پولیس نے گرفتار ڈاکو کے قبضے سے ایک پستول، گولیاں، موبائل فونز اور نقدی بھی برآمد کر لی ہے۔ قانون نافذ کرنے والے اداروں کی جانب سے مفرور ساتھی کی تلاش کے لیے کارروائی کا آغاز کر دیا گیا ہے۔

یہ کارروائی شہر میں بڑھتے ہوئے جرائم پر قابو پانے اور اسٹریٹ کرمنلز کے خلاف جاری مایکرو آپریشنز کا حصہ ہے تاکہ شہریوں کے جان و مال کا تحفظ یقینی بنایا جا سکے۔

stories.title: Federico Valverde Scores Late Winner as Real Madrid Beats AEK Athens
stories.summary:
Real Madrid secured a dramatic 3-2 victory against AEK Athens in the Champions League on Wednesday, courtesy of a stunning long-range strike from Federico Valverde in the 92nd minute. Managed by Jose Mourinho, the visiting team had to twice come from behind against the Greek champions. The win maintains Real Madrid's 100 percent start to the tournament, keeping them level with holders Paris Saint-Germain with four victories from four league phase games.

The hosts started the match with tremendous energy at the Agia Sophia stadium. Aboubakary Koita opened the scoring for AEK in the 12th minute after getting past Marc Cucurella. Real Madrid responded when Jude Bellingham equalized with a clever flick following a low cross from Cucurella. With fifteen minutes remaining, AEK regained the lead when Stavros Pilios scored through Thibaut Courtois's legs, assisted by Koita.

Kylian Mbappe quickly pulled Madrid level once again, netting his fourth Champions League goal of the season and his 16th across all competitions. Late in the match, substitute Endrick set up Mbappe, whose shot hit the crossbar after a sensational save by AEK goalkeeper Alberto Brignoli. However, Valverde ensured the visitors claimed all three points with his decisive late goal.

The victory marks Real Madrid's seventh consecutive win across all competitions. Mourinho's side displayed resilience throughout the match in the Greek capital, ultimately overcoming a tireless AEK Athens side to preserve their flawless record in Europe's premier club competition.

stories.title: کراچی: جناح گراؤنڈ کے قریب رینجرز اور پولیس کا مقابلہ، ایک ڈاکو ہلاک اور دو زخمی
stories.summary:
کراچی کے علاقے مزار قائد کے قریب جناح گراؤنڈ کے نزدیک بدھ اور جمعرات کی درمیانی شب رینجرز اور ایس آئی یو پولیس نے ایک مشترکہ کارروائی کی۔ اس دوران ہونے والے مبینہ پولیس مقابلے میں ایک ڈاکو ہلاک جبکہ دو زخمی حالت میں گرفتار کر لیے گئے۔

پولیس ترجمان کے مطابق ہلاک ہونے والے ملزم کی شناخت پینتیس سالہ زوہان ولد سلمان الدین کے طور پر ہوئی ہے۔ جبکہ زخمی حالت میں گرفتار ہونے والے دونوں ڈاکوؤں کی شناخت چوبیس سالہ حسن ولد شاہد اور چوبیس سالہ سید حسین ولد ارشاد کے ناموں سے کی گئی ہے۔ تمام ہلاک و زخمی افراد کو فوری طور پر جناح اسپتال منتقل کیا گیا۔

ابتدائی اطلاعات کے مطابق یہ تمام ملزمان بھتہ خوری سمیت دیگر سنگین جرائم کی متعدد وارداتوں میں ملوث رہے ہیں۔ قانون نافذ کرنے والے اداروں نے ان کے قبضے سے دو پستول، گولیاں، موبائل فونز، نقدی اور ایک موٹرسائیکل برآمد کر لی ہے۔

اس کامیاب کارروائی کے بعد سکیورٹی اداروں نے شہر بھر میں جرائم پیشہ عناصر کے خلاف گھیرا مزید تنگ کرنے اور قانون کی رٹ قائم رکھنے کے عزم کا اعادہ کیا ہے۔

stories.title: Pakistan Government Seeks Every Opportunity to Lower Fuel Prices
stories.summary:
Pakistan's Minister of State for Finance, Bilal Azhar Kiyani, stated that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif continuously explores every possible avenue to decrease petrol and diesel prices. In an exclusive statement to ARY News, Kiyani emphasized that the administration is working diligently to guarantee the supply of petroleum products at reduced rates. He assured that the country has experienced no fuel shortages.

To maintain stability, the prime minister established a specialized committee tasked with monitoring fuel supplies on a daily basis. Kiyani noted that this committee operates regularly and oversees every incoming oil cargo in accordance with the prime minister's explicit directives. Authorities are also keeping a close eye on domestic refinery production, overall fuel inventories, and the transportation logistics of petroleum products nationwide.

Furthermore, the government has instructed officials to constantly evaluate market conditions and acquire incoming oil shipments at the most affordable prices achievable. Kiyani highlighted that the administration's initiatives directly impact citizens, noting that 12 million people are currently receiving fuel subsidies through the prime minister's designated fuel scheme.

These ongoing monitoring efforts and subsidy programs form part of the government's broader strategy to manage energy costs and ease financial pressures on the public. The measures reflect the administration's stated commitment to maintaining stable fuel availability and pricing throughout the country.

stories.title: FIA Arrests Two Agents in Islamabad for Albania Visa Scam
stories.summary:
The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) Islamabad Zone arrested two agents accused of defrauding a citizen out of Rs 1.5 million under the false pretense of securing an Albanian work visa. An official announced on Wednesday that the operation was executed by the Anti-Human Trafficking Circle Rawalpindi, leading to the apprehension of suspects Ghulam Dastgir and Shahid Hussain in connection with FIR No. 647/2026.

According to investigators, the suspects took the substantial sum of money from the complainant after promising to facilitate his employment travel to Albania. Authorities are currently looking deeper into the specifics of the alleged fraud. Investigators are also working to identify and determine the potential involvement of any other individuals connected to the illegal scheme.

The inquiry into the matter is being led by Inspector Zainab Batool. The FIA Islamabad Zone emphasized its ongoing commitment to cracking down on human trafficking, visa fraud networks, and other related criminal enterprises.

This arrest highlights the continued efforts of law enforcement agencies in Pakistan to target fraudulent agents who exploit citizens seeking employment opportunities abroad. Investigations remain active as authorities work to dismantle the broader operation.

stories.title: Google Warns That LLMjacking Cyberattacks Are Costing Cloud AI Customers Dearly
stories.summary:
Cybercriminals are increasingly exploiting the rising popularity of artificial intelligence by hijacking corporate AI accounts and cloud credentials, a threat technique designated as LLMjacking by Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG). Unlike cryptojacking, which gradually increases expenses, LLMjacking can generate financial damages exceeding $100,000 within minutes. Bad actors typically initiate these campaigns by discovering vulnerable AI endpoints or by acquiring stolen application programming interface keys and cloud tokens, including GitHub personal access tokens, identity tokens, service account credentials, and active session tokens. 

Upon breaching a victim's network architecture, intruders seek to elevate their access privileges, secure persistent entry, and locate valuable artificial intelligence assets. Their primary objective is financial gain, achieved by executing unauthorized AI workloads, streaming models automatically, or reselling compromised system access to external buyers. According to Google, a specific threat cluster identified as UNC6993 amassed over $100,000 in cloud service charges after securing large language model API keys and activating projects inside a victim's cloud environment. In separate incidents, attackers enrolled hijacked accounts into pay-as-you-go programs, selected high-tier AI models, and launched massive inference workloads while monitoring billing dashboards and bypassing rate limits via temporary service accounts.

This malicious activity has evolved into a specialized branch of cybercrime, featuring distinct operational roles. While some threat actors focus exclusively on breaking into enterprise systems, specialized intermediaries known as LLM Mixers operate gateways that gather stolen credentials, route incoming requests, and commercialize unauthorized AI resources for underground clients. GTIG anticipates that LLMjacking will expand further alongside the broader market for artificial intelligence services.

To mitigate these risks, Google urges organizations to closely monitor their AI infrastructures and treat any unauthorized adjustments to platform accounts or settings as critical security incidents. Companies are strongly advised to enforce the principle of least privilege, ensuring that users and system accounts retain only the minimum permissions necessary for their operational functions.

stories.title: Sindh Government and State Bank Announce Public Holiday for Iqbal Day
stories.summary:
The Sindh government has officially declared a province-wide public holiday on Monday, November 9, 2026, to commemorate the birth anniversary of the renowned poet and philosopher Allama Muhammad Iqbal.
